pr_title: Handle libpq db version 0 as connection failure in `PostgreSQLAdapter`
pr_body:

About this template

The following template aims to help contributors write a good description for their pull requests.

Feel free to discard it if you need to (e.g. when you just fix a typo). -->

### Motivation / Background

<!--
Describe why this Pull Request needs to be merged. What bug have you fixed? What feature have you added? Why is it important?
If you are fixing a specific issue, include "Fixes #ISSUE" (replace with the issue number, remove the quotes) and the issue will be linked to this PR.
-->

Fixes https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/54712

### Detail

In `PostgreSQLAdapter`, if the database version returned by pg/libpq is 0, we now raise `ActiveRecord::ConnectionFailed` which:
1. more accurately tells the user that a connection failure has happened instead of a version incompatibility
2. ensures the version isn't cached so that subsequent re-connection attempts may retrieve the correct version with a successful connection

**Note:** I think this should also be back-ported to 7.2.

issue_context.title: `PostgreSQLAdapter` caches database version of 0 returned by libpq
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce

<!-- (Guidelines for creating a bug report are [available
here](https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#creating-a-bug-report)) -->

<!-- Paste your executable test case created from one of the scripts found [here](https://edgeguides.rubyonrails.org/contributing_to_ruby_on_rails.html#create-an-executable-test-case) below: -->

During a recent database fail-over we saw many errors like this:
```
RuntimeError: Your version of PostgreSQL (0) is too old. Active Record supports PostgreSQL >= 9.3.
```

We tracked it down to libpq returning 0 when asked to query the database version and when connection was bad:
- https://github.com/ged/ruby-pg/blob/62508cc14189653153c205a0c338066b90399834/ext/pg_connection.c#L869-L873
- https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/7f24c0274385ea3d4c797cc2fd60d9a55f3a8d74/src/interfaces/libpq/fe-connect.c#L7542-L7550

This then gets compared against the minimum version supported by `PostgreSQLAdapter`, and if incompatible an error is raised here: https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/3720ca0e29d2afaafea18258c7c41fcf909929d0/activerecord/lib/active_record/connection_adapters/postgresql_adapter.rb#L665-L669

This gets called at some point during `#configure_connection`.

Despite having had database fail-overs before, we've never seen this error until we upgraded to 7.2. I suspect it has something to do with https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/49415, possibly also in combination with https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/44570.

This error is fine as is, the issue is that the version of 0 gets cached and reused on subsequent `#configure_connection` calls i.e. during re-connections, which means the connection will never recover even if the database recovers and raw connections are successful: https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/3720ca0e29d2afaafea18258c7c41fcf909929d0/activerecord/lib/active_record/connection_adapters/abstract/connection_pool.rb#L30-L32

I don't have a reproduction script, but I've been able to replicate with a test which I've paired with a patch: https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/54713

### Expected behavior

<!-- Tell us what should happen -->

Following the error, re-connections to a healthy database with a valid version should succeed.

### Actual behavior

<!-- Tell us what happens instead -->

Following the error, re-connections to a healthy database with a valid version continue to raise the same error.

### System configuration

**Rails version**: 7.2.2.1

**Ruby version**: 3..3.7
comments: I merged, but IMO the `pg` gem should do the raising, given `libpq` is quite clear that a returned `0` is an error.

> I merged, but IMO the `pg` gem should do the raising, given `libpq` is quite clear that a returned `0` is an error.

Thank you. Yes I agree, I'll open an issue there and update here if anything comes out of it.

review_comments:
Without the patch, if I update the assertion above to expect [this](https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/049d1af38d19968fc8e8648989b0fb8aae2caa71/activerecord/lib/active_record/connection_adapters/postgresql_adapter.rb#L665-L669) `RuntimeError` and the respective message to pass, this assertion fails with:

![Screenshot 2025-03-08 at 12 08 10 am](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7b08baf8-5019-42f0-8abf-3ec0c0045e9b)

i.e. it cannot successfully reconnect and the same error is raised due to 0 being cached.

I wasn't sure what the appropriate error to use here was. I went with this over `ActiveRecord::ConnectionNotEstablished` only because of this snippet of code indicating the former is used for libpq related errors: https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/049d1af38d19968fc8e8648989b0fb8aae2caa71/activerecord/lib/active_record/connection_adapters/postgresql_adapter.rb#L804-L814

Note that libpq may return 0 either of there is no connection or if an existing connection is bad: https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/7f24c0274385ea3d4c797cc2fd60d9a55f3a8d74/src/interfaces/libpq/fe-connect.c#L7542-L7550
